paragraphs: The paper studies convex optimization in which the nonzero parts of a solution must follow a graph structure. Frank-Wolfe methods depend on an oracle that identifies a useful update direction. For these constraints, that oracle can be difficult to compute efficiently, making the quality and cost of approximate directions central to the method.

The authors show that two familiar approximation requirements, based on additive or multiplicative errors in the optimization gap, do not provide a cheap oracle here. They instead propose approximating an inner product through a dual maximization oracle. This changes the quantity being approximated so that the analysis can accommodate the graph constraints.

They establish convergence guarantees that depend on oracle accuracy and whether the constraint set is relaxed. A variant achieves a rate proportional to one over the squared iteration count when the solution lies on the boundary and a quadratic growth assumption holds. Image recovery experiments exhibit faster convergence than the bounds suggest, indicating that the worst-case analysis can be pessimistic.
icml-2022-approximate-frank-wolfe-algori.tldr: An alternative approximate oracle enables Frank-Wolfe methods for graph-structured constraints, with conditional convergence guarantees and promising image recovery results.

paragraphs: A label noise transition matrix describes how likely each clean label is to become each observed, corrupted label. Estimating this matrix can support statistically robust learning. Existing estimators often depend on especially reliable examples or well-separated groups in the feature representation, conditions that can fail when informative and uninformative features coexist.

The paper proposes reducing the influence of less informative parts of a representation before estimating the transition matrix. Its information-theoretic approach addresses a practical difficulty: deciding which features are informative when the available labels are themselves noisy. The authors prove that a measure called f-mutual information can often preserve its ordering even when calculated with noisy labels.

That ordering result supports building an estimator from the distilled features without first requiring clean labels for the information calculation. Evaluations on tabular and text classification tasks examine transition-matrix estimation error and demonstrate the method's effectiveness with lower-quality features. The contribution connects feature quality directly to noise estimation, while the ordering claim remains qualified rather than universal.
icml-2022-beyond-images-label-noise-tran.tldr: An information-theoretic method down-weights uninformative features to improve label noise transition estimates in tabular and text tasks.

paragraphs: Contextual bandit algorithms choose actions using information about the current situation and learn from the resulting feedback. Methods that work well with a small menu of actions can become difficult to use when the choices are extremely numerous or continuous. The paper targets this gap between flexible prediction models and efficient decision making.

The authors introduce a general-purpose algorithm for continuous action spaces with linear structure. It relies on two computational components: a supervised learning oracle and an oracle for optimization over the action space. Together, these components let the method use general-purpose models while handling action selection through a separate optimization operation.

The stated guarantees make sample complexity, runtime, and memory independent of the number of available actions. This is meaningful for continuous spaces, where enumerating every choice is impossible, but the result specifically concerns the stated linear structure and oracle access. A large-scale empirical evaluation finds that the method typically improves both performance and efficiency relative to standard baselines.
icml-2022-contextual-bandits-with-large-.tldr: An oracle-based contextual bandit algorithm handles continuous, linearly structured actions with complexity independent of action-space size.

paragraphs: Learning to choose among a vast or continuous set of actions creates difficulties for contextual bandits. Standard regret, which evaluates the cost of imperfect decisions, can be too demanding to guarantee efficiently in this setting. The paper develops an alternative evaluation criterion intended to support useful learning guarantees for such action spaces.

The proposed smooth regret notion dominates earlier alternatives. For this criterion, the authors give an algorithm that is efficient in both data use and computation while accommodating general function approximation through standard supervised learning oracles. They also introduce an adaptive algorithm that automatically adjusts to any smoothness level, extending the approach beyond a single fixed level.

The framework can recover previously established minimax or Pareto-optimal standard-regret guarantees in settings including multiple best actions and Lipschitz or Hölder bandits. Thus, the alternative criterion also connects to familiar guarantees in structured cases. Large-scale experiments support the algorithms' efficacy, complementing the theoretical account of when broad action spaces can be handled efficiently.
icml-2022-contextual-bandits-with-smooth.tldr: Smooth regret enables efficient contextual bandit algorithms for continuous actions, including an algorithm that adapts automatically to smoothness.

paragraphs: Self-supervised representation learning is often evaluated on carefully curated datasets, while real data can have a long tail of infrequent categories. Without labels, identifying those rare examples is difficult. This makes it harder to transfer supervised strategies that rebalance losses or redesign models around known category frequencies.

Boosted Contrastive Learning approaches the problem through the data used in contrastive learning. It uses neural networks' memorization behavior to automatically regulate the information discrepancy between different views of a sample. The learning signal therefore depends on how those views differ, with memorization helping drive that difference in a setting where category labels are unavailable.

The motivation is to improve long-tailed learning without relying on explicit discovery of rare labeled categories or heuristic architectural choices. Experiments across several benchmark datasets show that the approach is effective relative to several state-of-the-art methods. These results support the usefulness of manipulating sample-view information through memorization for the tested self-supervised learning problems.
icml-2022-contrastive-learning-with-boos.tldr: Boosted Contrastive Learning uses memorization to regulate differences between sample views and improve self-supervised learning on long-tailed data.

paragraphs: Counterfactual prediction estimates what outcome a treatment would produce, including treatments that were not actually taken. Many learning objectives seek accurate predictions across the entire treatment space. The paper argues that this can misalign with decision making, where attention often centers on a small set of treatments capable of producing especially good outcomes.

The authors define an objective focused on these outcome-oriented treatments and introduce Outcome-Oriented Sample Re-weighting. The method changes the influence of training samples so that the predictor concentrates more on promising treatments. This objective mismatch becomes especially consequential when many choices are available, as in a continuous treatment space.

The theoretical analysis shows that the method can improve treatment selection toward the optimal choice. Experiments using synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets support its effectiveness. The central contribution is to connect predictive training more closely to the decision it supports: errors around promising options can matter differently from errors spread across all possible treatments.
icml-2022-counterfactual-prediction-for-.tldr: Outcome-Oriented Sample Re-weighting focuses counterfactual prediction on promising treatments to improve treatment selection.

paragraphs: Incorrect labels can teach neural networks misleading relationships. Detecting those labels through model training creates a difficulty: the model may itself memorize the corruption. This paper instead studies detection directly from neighborhood relationships in the available features, avoiding the need to train a predictive model for that detection task.

The first method uses local voting, checking whether an example's noisy label agrees with labels of nearby examples. It rests on the intuition that nearby feature representations are more likely to share a clean label. The second method ranks examples by a score and filters a guaranteed number of examples considered likely to be corrupted; this does not imply every filtered label is wrong.

The authors analyze how feature quality affects local voting, give guidance for choosing neighborhood size, and establish a worst-case error bound for ranking. Experiments with synthetic and real-world noise report consistent, substantial improvements over most training-based baselines. The findings make neighborhood information a useful basis for label inspection when its relationship to clean labels is informative.
icml-2022-detecting-corrupted-labels-wit.tldr: Feature-neighborhood voting and ranking detect corrupted labels without training a predictive model for detection.

paragraphs: Adversarial inputs can cause neural networks to make incorrect predictions. This paper investigates that vulnerability by asking which parts of an input are statistically associated with the model's output. It separates dependence on natural patterns from dependence on adversarial patterns, using estimated mutual information to quantify each relationship.

The authors observe that adversarial examples usually have greater adversarial mutual information and lower natural mutual information than natural examples. They turn this observation into a training objective: increase dependence between predictions and natural patterns while reducing dependence between predictions and adversarial patterns. The intended effect is to direct the model toward patterns carrying the input's meaningful content.

Empirical evaluations show improved adversarial accuracy against multiple attacks. The finding supports mutual-information estimation as a useful training signal for the evaluated defenses. The distinction between observation and intention matters: the information pattern is reported as typical, and greater attention to natural semantics is the expected mechanism, rather than a universal guarantee about every trained model.
icml-2022-improving-adversarial-robustne.tldr: Training to increase natural-pattern mutual information and reduce adversarial-pattern mutual information improves accuracy against multiple evaluated attacks.

paragraphs: Inductive matrix completion seeks to reconstruct a low-rank matrix from a limited set of observed entries, using prior knowledge about its row and column subspaces. The paper addresses both the structure of this optimization problem and the practical task of solving it quickly with reliable recovery.

The authors prove that, under suitable conditions, the optimization landscape contains no bad local minima. They also provide a simple procedure with theoretical guarantees for estimating the unknown matrix's rank. These contributions address two distinct uncertainties: whether local optimization can encounter undesirable minima, and how to choose the rank needed for reconstruction.

Their proposed solver, GNIMC, uses a Gauss-Newton method. Its recovery guarantees improve on other methods in several respects, including quadratic convergence, fewer required observations, and stability when observations contain errors or the matrix deviates from low rank. With entries sampled uniformly at random, experiments show substantially faster recovery than several competitors. The landscape and recovery claims retain their stated conditional character.
icml-2022-inductive-matrix-completion-no.tldr: The paper establishes conditional landscape guarantees for inductive matrix completion and introduces a fast Gauss-Newton solver with strong recovery guarantees.

paragraphs: This paper studies adversarial noise through the relationship between the labels used to generate attacks and the correct labels of the original data. Its motivation is that adversarial noise contains features that generalize, and relationships between adversarial and natural data can help infer the natural data and support reliable predictions.

The method introduces an instance-dependent transition matrix. Here, adversarial labels are the flipped labels used when generating adversarial examples, while natural labels are the original ground truth. The matrix relates these two label types separately for each instance, allowing the modeled relationship to vary across examples instead of treating it as a single shared transition.

The transition matrix can be embedded in the target model, which the authors describe as enabling the modeling of stronger adaptive adversarial noise. Empirical evaluations show that the method can improve adversarial accuracy. The contribution is therefore an explicit model of the attack-label relationship, with experimental support for using that relationship to improve predictions under adversarial perturbations.
icml-2022-modeling-adversarial-noise-for.tldr: An instance-dependent transition matrix models relationships between adversarial and natural labels to improve adversarial accuracy.

paragraphs: Answering a logical query on a knowledge graph can require several connected reasoning steps. Symbolic traversal makes those steps interpretable but relies on the graph's recorded links. Neural approaches can reason with incomplete graphs, yet their internal representation of a query can be difficult to inspect.

Graph Neural Network Query Executor combines these approaches by breaking a query into relation projections and logical operations on fuzzy sets. The intermediate variables remain interpretable through these sets. A graph neural network adapted from knowledge graph completion performs the relation projections, allowing the system to reason about missing links, while product fuzzy logic handles the logical operations.

Experiments on three datasets show significant improvements over previous state-of-the-art methods for answering first-order logic queries. The model can also predict how many answers a query has without explicit supervision for that quantity and visualize intermediate variables. These capabilities connect answer quality with visibility into the reasoning process, supporting inspection of intermediate results alongside the final answer.
icml-2022-neural-symbolic-models-for-log.tldr: GNN-QE combines neural link reasoning with fuzzy logical operations to answer complex queries while exposing interpretable intermediate results.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations combine a learned model with a numerical solver for differential equations. The solver affects model performance, raising a basic question: what equation does training actually recover? This paper introduces inverse modified differential equations to characterize the influence of numerical integration on the learning process.

An inverse modified differential equation is determined jointly by the learning task and the chosen solver. The authors show that a trained Neural ODE closely approximates this modified equation, rather than the true underlying equation. This distinction explains why fitting the training task well does not, by itself, identify the underlying dynamics independently of the integration method.

The analysis bounds the discrepancy from the true equation by the sum of discretization error and learning loss. It also establishes a theoretical failure to learn conservation laws when using non-symplectic integration. Numerical experiments support the analysis. Together, these findings make the numerical solver part of the model's learned behavior, with consequences for both accuracy and conservation properties.
icml-2022-on-numerical-integration-in-ne.tldr: Inverse modified differential equations explain how numerical solvers shape the dynamics learned by Neural ODEs and affect conservation laws.

paragraphs: Coreset selection aims to replace a full training dataset with a weighted subset that yields similar model performance. Selecting that subset is a discrete optimization problem. Existing approaches for large models often use greedy search, which can become expensive as the subset grows and can produce suboptimal selections.

The paper replaces direct subset search with a continuous probabilistic formulation that learns a selection weight for each training example. Its two-level procedure samples coresets and trains the model to convergence in the inner loop. The outer loop then adjusts the sampling probabilities according to the resulting model performance, linking selection decisions to how well the selected data supports learning.

The authors develop an efficient solver using unbiased policy gradients, avoiding implicit differentiation, and prove convergence of the training procedure. Experiments report better results than various coreset selection methods across multiple tasks, especially with noisy labels and class imbalance. The contribution is a way to learn a distribution over useful subsets through their training outcomes.
icml-2022-probabilistic-bilevel-coreset-.tldr: A probabilistic bilevel method learns which training examples to sample, improving coreset selection especially under label noise and class imbalance.

paragraphs: Controlling a generated image through a GAN's latent representation often means finding directions associated with meaningful visual changes. Existing methods either emphasize whole-image attributes or use segmentation annotations to discover local attributes. This paper addresses semantic discovery for an arbitrary image region in a pretrained GAN.

The authors formulate regional semantic discovery as a dual optimization problem. An appropriately constructed generalized Rayleigh quotient provides a way to solve that problem without additional training or annotations. The approach works with semantics already learned by the generator, making the chosen region central to the discovery of useful latent controls.

Experiments across several state-of-the-art GAN models demonstrate effective regional manipulation. The authors report advantages over previous approaches in precision of control, robustness with respect to regions, implementation speed, and ease of use. These findings support the method as an efficient way to expose local editing capabilities in pretrained generators, with the no-training claim applying to semantic discovery rather than the original GAN.
icml-2022-region-based-semantic-factoriz.tldr: A regional optimization method discovers local semantic controls in pretrained GANs without annotations or additional training.

paragraphs: Outlier-robust principal component analysis seeks to recover the underlying subspace of clean data despite the presence of outliers. The online setting adds a practical constraint: examples arrive sequentially, and the algorithm must recover that subspace with only one pass through the data. This changes what information is available while making processing decisions.

The paper's central technique is a robust version of the residual norm. Informally, it considers both how important a data point is and how likely it is to behave as an outlier. This combination is useful because a point's relevance to subspace recovery must be considered alongside the possibility that it represents contamination.

The authors provide a provable online algorithm with a recovery guarantee comparable to the best known batch algorithm, while substantially improving on previous online methods. The comparison concerns recovery guarantees, bringing the stated reliability of one-pass processing closer to that of methods operating on a batch. The contribution centers on this theoretical result and the robust residual-based sampling technique enabling it.
icml-2022-residual-based-sampling-for-on.tldr: Robust residual-based sampling gives a one-pass outlier-robust PCA algorithm with recovery guarantees comparable to the best known batch method.

paragraphs: Federated learning uses data distributed across devices, but devices and their connections can differ substantially. Heterogeneous systems and uncertain wireless transmission can increase communication costs and delay convergence. This paper proposes a learning scheme that addresses differences between devices and incomplete communication within a shared model design.

Devices learn self-distilled neural networks whose knowledge is organized in a nested, progressive manner. These networks can be pruned to arbitrary sizes, allowing different devices to use varying model architectures. The organization also allows part of the model parameters to be transmitted when a connection is faulty, while retaining the useful knowledge contributed by the transmitted portion.

This connects model flexibility with communication resilience: the same nested structure supports differently sized models and partial transfers. Extensive empirical studies under system heterogeneity and network instability show significant resilience and higher communication efficiency than state-of-the-art alternatives. The findings support using progressively organized model knowledge to make federated learning more practical under the evaluated device and network conditions.
icml-2022-resilient-and-communication-ef.tldr: Nested, self-distilled models support different device capabilities and useful partial transmissions, improving federated learning under unstable connections.

paragraphs: Visualizing high-dimensional data in fewer dimensions requires reconciling spaces with different geometric properties. The crowding problem reflects a mismatch in how much room those spaces provide for representing relationships among points. SpaceMAP addresses this mismatch through an analytical transformation of distance metrics between the original and visualization spaces.

The method introduces an equivalent extended distance intended to match the capacities of high- and low-dimensional spaces in a principled way. It also uses hierarchical manifold approximation to construct a similarity function tailored to the data. This second component accommodates datasets whose underlying manifolds have different properties, rather than treating their geometry identically.

Evaluations on synthetic and real datasets with varied manifold properties report strong performance relative to classical and state-of-the-art dimensionality reduction methods. Beyond the particular algorithm, the authors present space expansion as a general framework for understanding nonlinear visualization methods, including t-SNE and UMAP. The contribution therefore combines a visualization procedure with an account of the geometric mismatch such procedures must manage.
icml-2022-spacemap-visualizing-high-dime.tldr: SpaceMAP transforms distances and adapts similarities to data geometry to address crowding in high-dimensional data visualization.

paragraphs: Decentralized stochastic gradient descent distributes training across communicating workers. This paper examines how the pattern of connections between those workers affects stability and generalization. The analysis concerns the consensus model and allows an optimization setting that is both non-convex and non-smooth.

The authors derive an expected stability bound involving total sample size, worker count, and a spectral quantity measuring network connectivity. They then obtain an average generalization bound that remains informative even when the spectral gap is small. Earlier analysis of a projected version of the algorithm had suggested uninformative bounds in this weakly connected regime.

The theory indicates a positive relationship between generalization and the spectral gap, and explains why controlling consensus early in training can improve generalization. Experiments with VGG-11 and ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet support the analysis. The result connects the communication network to predictive behavior beyond the training data, rather than assessing network structure solely through its effect on optimization.
icml-2022-topology-aware-generalization-.tldr: Topology-aware stability bounds connect decentralized SGD's generalization to network connectivity and explain benefits of early consensus control.

paragraphs: Imitation learning often aims to match or surpass average human performance. When demonstrations vary in quality and the best examples are difficult to identify, that objective can hinder expert-level behavior. This paper instead seeks behavior that dominates all demonstrations or falls short of that goal as little as possible.

The proposed inverse optimal control objective minimizes subdominance. High-quality demonstrations primarily determine the objective, while lower-quality demonstrations are more easily dominated and therefore effectively ignored. This provides a way to handle mixed-quality demonstrations without allowing easier-to-surpass behavior to degrade the imitation target.

The authors state that, with increasing probability, the approach produces behavior with lower cost than demonstrations under the demonstrator's unknown cost function, even when that function differs between demonstrations. On a computer cursor pointing task, they report 78% superhuman behavior, compared with 50% for minimizing demonstration suboptimality and 72% after selective data cleaning. These task-specific findings support the objective's ability to exploit mixed-quality demonstrations; they do not establish uniformly superhuman autonomy across tasks.
icml-2022-towards-uniformly-superhuman-a.tldr: Minimizing subdominance emphasizes stronger demonstrations and yields more superhuman behavior in the evaluated cursor pointing task.

paragraphs: Vision Transformers have shown strong resistance to various image corruptions, with self-attention considered part of the explanation. This paper investigates how self-attention contributes to robust representations. Its motivation comes from visual grouping properties suggesting that attention could improve intermediate visual representations and, through them, robustness.

The authors propose fully attentional networks, a family of architectures that uses self-attention for both token mixing and channel processing. This extends attention across two kinds of representation processing. They evaluate the design across different hierarchical backbones, connecting their investigation of attention with a concrete architectural proposal.

A model using a DeiT architecture achieves a reported state-of-the-art mean corruption error of 47.6% on ImageNet-C with 29 million parameters. The authors also demonstrate significantly improved robustness in semantic segmentation and object detection. These findings support the proposed attention design across classification and downstream vision tasks, while the suggested role of visual grouping remains the motivating explanation for the architectural changes.
icml-2022-understanding-the-robustness-i.tldr: Fully attentional networks apply self-attention to token and channel processing, improving measured robustness across several vision tasks.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can perform well on downstream tasks whose images were already present during pretraining. Such overlap may overstate how well the models generalize to unfamiliar images. The paper also identifies a second evaluation gap: focusing on absolute task performance can overlook the efficiency required to achieve it.

VLUE evaluates models across multiple tasks and dimensions, combining generalization testing with the efficiency-performance trade-off. Its out-of-distribution test sets use images from a more diverse distribution spanning cultures. The benchmark's Pareto perspective considers performance alongside efficiency, making resource trade-offs part of how model progress is assessed.

All evaluated vision-language pretraining models show a sizable generalization gap on the out-of-distribution tests. Assessing efficiency together with performance also provides complementary insights into model design choices. The benchmark therefore broadens the evidence used to judge progress: strong results on familiar image distributions are considered alongside transfer to diverse imagery and the practical efficiency of achieving those results.
icml-2022-vlue-a-multi-task-multi-dimens.tldr: VLUE evaluates vision-language models on diverse unseen-image distributions and efficiency-performance trade-offs, revealing substantial generalization gaps.

paragraphs: The paper develops gradient-based methods for maximizing partial AUC in deep learning. It covers both one-way and two-way versions of the objective. Its central move is to formulate surrogate objectives through distributionally robust optimization, using that framework to define a loss for each individual positive example.

Two formulations offer different optimization properties. One uses conditional value at risk and yields an exact but non-smooth estimator of partial AUC. The other uses a KL-divergence-regularized robust objective and yields a smooth but inexact estimator. This makes the relationship between fidelity to the target quantity and smoothness of the optimization objective explicit.

The authors provide algorithms for the two formulations in both partial-AUC settings and establish convergence guarantees for optimizing them. These guarantees concern the proposed non-convex optimization procedures, without asserting that every run reaches a global optimum. Experiments on various datasets demonstrate the methods' effectiveness for deep learning, supporting the robust-optimization formulations as practical routes to partial-AUC maximization.
icml-2022-when-auc-meets-dro-optimizing-.tldr: Distributionally robust formulations enable gradient-based partial-AUC optimization with exact non-smooth or approximate smooth objectives and convergence guarantees.

paragraphs: Graph clustering through multicut groups nodes according to costs associated with separating them. Sparse formulations require specifying which graph connections exist. ClusterFuG instead uses a complete graph, avoiding that topology choice while retaining weighted costs that are more expressive than those of unweighted correlation clustering.

A complete graph ordinarily creates at least quadratic representation and computation costs for multicut methods. The paper represents the dense clustering objective through inner products of node feature vectors. This factorization supports a more efficient formulation and inference, making a fully connected objective practical without treating every pairwise cost as an independently represented quantity.

The authors adapt classical greedy multicut algorithms to this dense setting and modify them to improve efficiency and solution quality. Their algorithms scale to graphs with tens of thousands of nodes. Experiments on Cityscapes instance segmentation and ImageNet clustering support the approach's merits. The contribution joins the modeling simplicity of full connectivity with a representation designed to reduce its computational burden.
icml-2023-clusterfug-clustering-fully-co.tldr: ClusterFuG factorizes weighted complete-graph clustering costs to make multicut inference practical for tens of thousands of nodes.

paragraphs: The paper considers selecting a distribution from a collection of candidates using samples from an unknown target distribution. The candidates share a discrete domain. The challenge has two separate scales: the number of possible domain values and the number of candidate distributions that could match the target.

The main result is a data structure that uses a number of target samples sublinear in the domain size and identifies a close candidate in time sublinear in the number of candidates. This combines a statistical saving with a computational one. The stated sample and query-time improvements concern different quantities, making their simultaneous achievement the central theoretical contribution.

The authors also improve an earlier algorithm whose running time is linear in the candidate count. Experiments evaluate this latter algorithm and show a substantial reduction in operations needed to reach a given accuracy compared with prior work. Thus, the paper offers both a sublinear-time data-structure result and experimental evidence for a separate, improved linear-time approach.
icml-2023-data-structures-for-density-es.tldr: A density-estimation data structure combines sublinear sample use with sublinear candidate search, while a separate linear-time algorithm improves empirical efficiency.

paragraphs: Logical learning tasks can contain so many combinations that representative training coverage is difficult. This paper studies generalization on the unseen, a strong out-of-distribution setting for Boolean functions. Success in this setting provides an initial view of extrapolation or reasoning when the training examples do not adequately represent the combinations encountered later.

The authors investigate networks trained with gradient descent or stochastic gradient descent. They provide theoretical and experimental evidence that certain instances of Transformers, random feature models, and diagonal linear networks learn minimum-degree interpolators on unseen inputs. This identifies a preference for particular low-degree solutions among functions compatible with the training data.

Other model instances, including some using larger learning rates or mean-field networks, show evidence of leaky minimum-degree solutions. The findings help explain length generalization and motivate Degree-Curriculum, which learns monomials more efficiently by progressively increasing their supports. The conclusions distinguish architecture and training settings, rather than claiming that every neural network exhibits the same extrapolation behavior.
icml-2023-generalization-on-the-unseen-l.tldr: Evidence of low-degree extrapolation in certain networks motivates a curriculum that learns monomials by progressively increasing their supports.
